description: Pane layout rules shared by the Mac (PaneLayoutTree, PaneLayoutTreeMutation, PaneLayoutState, PaneLayoutMinimumSize, PaneLayoutGeometry) and the desktop client (soyeht_client::layout). Trees are the protocol layout nodes. Both pass every case. Where a pane goes that the tree does not list (`arrange`) is shared too: by role, primary panes left to right and auxiliary panes stacked on the right. Dragging a divider (`resize`: the split's path, the divider after child `dividerIndex`, the distance in points, positive to the right or down, and the viewport) changes only the two weights beside it, keeps their sum, and stops at the floors of what is beside it; a window with no room beyond the floors changes nothing; `equalize` gives the children equal shares of what they can have above their floors; a null `expected` is a refusal. Dragging a pane by its header onto another is fixed by `dropZone` (a point on a pane's rectangle and the zone it lands on: the edge within `edgeFraction` of it, the nearest edge on a corner, else the center, none outside), `dropZoneRect` (the part of the pane a zone covers) and `move` (the pane to move, the target pane and the zone; the tree it becomes, and null when a pane is not in the tree). Each case gives the floors to weigh with (the file's floor for a kind it does not list), a stored layout and the live panes in workspace order.

kindFloors.description: The measured floor of every kind of pane, for the font metrics the accepted floor report used (PaneLayoutFloorFormula on the Mac, pane_floors on the desktop; both pass every case). `surfaces` holds [width, height] of the pane without the card halo, with the editor's project panel open; `compactSurfaces` holds the kinds that fold optional chrome away when the person hides it (the editor without its project panel). The Mac measures its fonts, the desktop takes the same metrics as the `reference*` tokens of design-tokens.json (the test of the token file keeps them equal to `fonts`). The agent's width is the one place the desktop may be wider than the Mac: it never draws a floor below the composer an agent pane always shows (views::composer::minimum_pane_width), and `desktopAgentWidth` bounds that composer width. `editorPreview` fixes when an editor shows the Markdown preview: the width of its text area (the editor without the project panel) and whether the preview shows.
